body.statement: Let \(\mathfrak R\) be a valid effective input with rational \(\alpha,\gamma,\zeta,\overline\varepsilon_n\), total interval oracles for \(p,b,v_{\min},v_{\max},p_{\min},\beta,\varepsilon_n\), rational-box representations of every optimized \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(V\in\mathcal K_V\), and \(\varepsilon_n\le\overline\varepsilon_n\) with \(\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}+\gamma<\alpha\). The algorithm \(\mathsf A(\mathfrak R)\) halts after at most \(N_{\mathsf A}\) certified box operations and oracle calls of precision at most \(m_{\mathsf A}\), and returns \((Q^+_{n,\alpha},\mathcal E_n,\mathfrak C)\). An exact-rational verifier accepts \(\mathfrak C\) only after checking every elementary-function, spectral, path, and Gaussian-probability outward enclosure, the inequalities \(\omega_t+\omega_h+\omega_V\le\zeta\) and \(\omega_{\mathrm{tail}}+\omega_{\mathrm{int}}+\omega_{\mathrm{fp}}\le\gamma\), and the branch-specific rational conditions in the calibration-certificate definition. Every accepted certificate implies \(\inf_{h\in\mathcal H,V\in\mathcal K_V}P\{S(h,Z_V)\le Q^+_{n,\alpha}+\zeta\}\ge1-\alpha+\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}\). This implication is valid for the refined branch and for the rational fallback \(Q^+_{n,\alpha}=2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\), including when the least-favorable law has atoms. Counting each interval primitive at unit cost, the bit complexity is polynomial in \(N_{\mathsf A}\), the maximum input bit length, and the oracle-output bit length at \(m_{\mathsf A}\).
body.justification: A critical value is operationally honest only when its real inputs have effective names, its rounding direction can be checked independently, and its worst-case running time is finite.
body.gap: Genz and Miwa supply integration engines for supplied rectangles or orthants, and Wang--Kennedy self-validates rectangular probabilities; none proves termination for this nonlinear continuum event or least-favorable parameter envelope.
body.consumer: The algorithm turns the asymptotic path law into an auditable critical value for low-dimensional multiaction experiments.
